skills.name: Savannah soils, animal life and human activity

note.text: Savannah soils vary with parent material, drainage, weathering and organic inputs; there is no single uniformly fertile savannah soil. Seasonal water availability affects decomposition, plant growth and grazing resources. Herbivores feed on vegetation and predators depend on prey; movements may follow seasonal food and water, but differ by species and barriers. Farming and livestock keeping use these environments, while excessive pressure can reduce cover and increase erosion. Protected areas also support conservation and tourism, with outcomes requiring local management.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to connect seasonal resources to soils wildlife and land use and balance a stated water store. Builds on: savannah seasonality and soil properties. Leads to: monsoon environments and Cameroon’s regional contrasts.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Northern Cameroon provides a setting for examining seasonal grazing, cultivation and conservation. A simple root-zone water account tracks an opening store, rainfall and stated losses. It is a classroom model, not an irrigation schedule. Soil texture, rooting depth and runoff affect actual water availability, while land rights, disease, markets and conservation requirements also influence real activities.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Explain the sequence from seasonal rain to vegetation and resource availability, then consider animal or human responses. Do not assume every animal migrates, all farmers share one method or every soil is identical. For the model account, label inputs and outputs before calculation; a mathematical balance does not alone justify a real land-use decision.

questions.prompt: A simplified savannah root-zone store begins with {start} mm. Rain adds {rain} mm; stated combined plant/evaporation losses remove {use} mm and drainage removes {drain} mm. With no other flows, find the final store.

misconceptions.explain: That treats losses as additional inputs.
That omits the stated drainage loss.
That repeats rainfall instead of balancing the store.

solution: Final store = opening store + input − the stated outputs.
{start} + {rain} − {use} − {drain} = {answer} mm. This model omits other possible flows.
